messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:
The patient, an 83-year-old woman with a history of developmental disorders, presented to the emergency outpatient unit with a one-week history of dyspnea. She had heavily decreased breath sounds in the left lung. Chest radiograph and CT scan of the chest showed pleural effusions on the left lung. Two diagnostic thoracenteses were non-diagnostic, and a semirigid thoracoscopy was performed to visualize the pleura. Thoracoscopy revealed diffuse thickening of the parietal and visceral pleura, compatible with pleural dissemination with biopsy samples taken from only the visceral pleura node. Hematoxylin and eosin staining and immunohistochemical staining revealed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma with malignant neoplasm. 
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Disposition:
The patient was discharged to the care of her family. 

Condition:
The patient had a stable condition upon discharge. 

Clinical Course:
The patient required semirigid thoracoscopy with biopsy samples taken from only the visceral pleura node. Hematoxylin and eosin staining and immunohistochemical staining revealed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma.

Follow-up:
The patient was referred for follow-up care with an oncologist. 

Instructions:
The patient was instructed to follow-up with an oncologist. 

Treatment:
The patient underwent semirigid thoracoscopy for biopsy samples, which was successful. The treatment plan includes referral to an oncologist for further management. 

Complications:
No complications were noted during the hospitalization.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The admission was to investigate a left pleural effusion, and thoracoscopic biopsy established lung adenocarcinoma with pleural dissemination, so the primary lung cancer is chiefly responsible. Primary malignancy takes precedence over the pleural spread and the effusion, placing it in chapter C (neoplasms). The category for malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung is C34.

CODE: C34
